executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with pandemic spillover potential, a resurgent dengue season with historically elevated case counts, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with RSV co-circulation. Mpox continues to spread in the Americas region while pertussis is demonstrating a notable resurgence across multiple countries, suggesting waning vaccine immunity or coverage gaps.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous epidemic threats are active across the Americas and Europe, with Avian Influenza A(H5N1) zoonotic spillover risk and record dengue transmission representing the highest-priority concerns requiring immediate coordinated response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained regional spread
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from ongoing animal reservoir activity
Dual PAHO alerts suggest escalating geographic spread across the Americas
threats.action: Activate enhanced surveillance at human-animal interfaces, enforce biosafety protocols at poultry and dairy farm operations, pre-position antiviral stockpiles, and conduct zoonotic exposure monitoring for farm workers and veterinary personnel

threats.name: Dengue
signals: February 2026 epidemiological update indicates active and potentially record-breaking transmission season
Historical patterns suggest peak season activity during Southern Hemisphere summer months preceding the alert
Multiple serotype co-circulation increases risk of severe dengue and hemorrhagic fever
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations, activate dengue early warning systems, ensure hospital surge capacity for severe dengue cases, and coordinate cross-border surveillance with national health authorities

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza / RSV Co-circulation
signals: January 2026 alert on simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation creating dual respiratory burden
April 2026 alert marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season indicating seasonal transition
December 2025 alert on end of Southern Hemisphere 2025 season and start of Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season suggests continuous hemispheric burden
threats.action: Accelerate influenza vaccination campaigns ahead of Southern Hemisphere season, strengthen RSV surveillance and pediatric hospital preparedness, and issue public health advisories on respiratory disease prevention

threats.name: Mpox
signals: April 2026 epidemiological update indicates ongoing transmission in the Americas
Sustained regional spread requiring continued PAHO monitoring suggests failure to achieve containment
Risk of clade expansion or importation events from high-burden regions
threats.action: Reinforce ring vaccination strategies, enhance contact tracing and case isolation, monitor for clade Ib importation events, and sustain diagnostic capacity across the region

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Dual epidemiological updates in December 2025 and March 2026 indicate persistent and resurging transmission
Multi-month alert cycle suggests inadequate vaccine coverage or waning immunity at population level
Risk to unvaccinated infants and immunocompromised individuals is high
threats.action: Audit vaccination coverage rates by country, implement catch-up immunization campaigns, promote Tdap booster for pregnant women and close contacts of infants, and strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: March 2026 epidemiological alert indicates active transmission risk or confirmed cases in the region
Sylvatic cycle activity in non-vaccinated populations poses outbreak ignition risk
Risk of urban cycle re-establishment in Aedes aegypti-endemic areas
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk zones, deploy emergency vaccination campaigns in affected areas, strengthen epizootic surveillance in non-human primates, and enforce travel vaccination requirements

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: February 2026 epidemiological alert indicates active chikungunya transmission
Co-circulation with dengue and Zika viruses in Aedes-endemic zones complicates clinical differentiation
Potential for geographic expansion into new territories with competent vectors
threats.action: Enhance arboviral syndromic surveillance, strengthen vector control measures, train clinicians on differential diagnosis of arboviral febrile illness, and monitor for neurological complications

threats.name: Measles
signals: February 2026 epidemiological alert signals measles transmission risk or confirmed cases in the region
COVID-19 pandemic-era immunization gaps have left susceptible cohorts across the region
Risk of imported cases seeding community outbreaks in under-vaccinated populations
threats.action: Conduct supplementary immunization activities targeting zero-dose and under-vaccinated children, strengthen measles surveillance and laboratory confirmation, and implement rapid response protocols for suspected cases

amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis resurgence across two consecutive reporting periods may reflect macrolide treatment failures or evolving antimicrobial resistance in addition to vaccine escape, warranting susceptibility testing
Sustained bacterial pathogen circulation in regions with high antibiotic use pressure increases selection for resistant strains in co-circulating pathogens
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (February 2026) may indicate counterfeit pharmaceutical supply chains that could also harbor subtherapeutic antibiotic formulations
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory burden (Influenza + RSV + COVID-19 variants) is creating compounded healthcare system strain across both hemispheres
Arboviral convergence zone in the Americas with concurrent Dengue, Chikungunya, and Yellow Fever alerts suggests Aedes vector populations are highly active and geographically expanding

Dual Avian Influenza A(H5N1) alert cadence (November 2025 and March 2026) indicates the virus is maintaining persistent enzootic presence rather than episodic incursions, elevating pandemic preparedness urgency
Pertussis resurgence across consecutive reporting periods points to a regional waning immunity cycle consistent with 3-5 year post-vaccination waning patterns observed globally
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly communicable disease threat reports (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) suggests a period of heightened multi-threat monitoring in Europe
Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) signals potential illicit alcohol supply contamination events that may be recurring or geographically expanding
